records.explanation: Turing shows that there can be no machine R which, applied to the S.D of an arbitrary machine M, determines whether M ever prints a given symbol, say 0. The proof proceeds by constructing machines M1, M2, ... which print the same sequence as M except that the first, first two, and so on occurrences of 0 are replaced by another symbol. A machine F writes down successively the S.D of M, M1, M2, .... Combining F with a hypothetical R gives a machine G which prints :0: if and only if the tested machine never prints 0. Testing G with R, if G never prints 0 then M prints 0 infinitely often; if G prints 0 sometimes then M does not print 0 infinitely often. Similarly for 1, and combining the processes decides whether M prints infinitely many figures, i.e. whether M is circle-free. Since no machine decides circle-freeness, no machine R exists. This result is then used in the reduction of the Entscheidungsproblem.
